Career talk · Final-year CS
From Writing Code to Engineering Solutions
Al Amru Bil Maruf · Software Engineer II, Synesis IT PLC
“Developer” is a family of jobs
Backend
APIs, business logic, databases. What happens after you click.
Frontend
What users see and touch, on every screen size.
QA
Breaks things before customers do.
UX / UI
Designs how it works for a human, before any code.
DevOps
Gets code to production and keeps it running.
DBA
Owns the data: speed, backups, safety.
SecOps
Thinks like an attacker, so the company doesn’t learn the hard way.
None is “better.” They’re different kinds of problems.
Which path should I choose?
You find out by doing, not by thinking
A button looks broken on mobile, and you can’t stop fixing it.
→ maybe frontend
A query takes five seconds, and you need to know why.
→ maybe backend
Notice which problems you enjoy being stuck on.

Pick one track. Go deep.
Backend
One language, one framework, one database. Until you can build without help.
or
Frontend
One framework, real layouts, real state. Until you can build without help.
Master one, and your second stack takes weeks, not months.
Escape tutorial hell
Following a tutorial feels like progress. You’re borrowing someone else’s thinking.
Getting stuck isn’t failure. It’s where the learning happens.
Any experience is experience
Your first job teaches you real teams, real codebases, real deadlines. That transfers anywhere. It’s a starting point, not a life sentence.
Investment
Long hours somewhere you’re learning a lot. This is the age to do it, while you have the energy.
Being used
Long hours repeating the same thing, for very little. Know the difference.
A story
What breaks between 10 requests and 10,000?
Live demo
One button. One real API call.
Open DevTools first, then switch to the Network tab.
Load products
GET https://dummyjson.com/products?limit=5&select=title,price
Now press refresh. Again. And again. Every refresh is a new request.


Live demo
Should every refresh hit the database?


Things that break in Production
01
Connection limits
The pool runs out. “Correct” code still fails.
→ SQL & databases
02
The double payment
The same request arrives twice. Did you charge twice?
→ Idempotency
03
Attacks
Bots start probing within hours of going live.
→ Networking
04
Monitoring
Know it’s broken before your users tell you.
→ Logs & alerts
Plus availability, testing, maintainability. None of it is in the tutorial. All of it is the job.


A loop inside a loop, O(n²), hides at small scale
10 records
100 steps
100,000 records
10 billion steps
DSA isn’t just for interviews. It decides whether your system scales or falls over.


If you remember one list from today
The fundamentals never to skip
DSA
So your code survives 10,000× more data.
SQL
Connections, indexes, slow queries, transactions.
Networking
You can’t defend what you don’t understand.


The question in the room
Will AI take my job?


AI types. You decide.
01
You direct
You tell it what to build, and how.
02
You judge
Is the answer actually right? Will it survive 10k requests?
03
You own it
When it breaks in production, it’s on you, not the AI.
Use AI heavily. Never ship code you can’t explain.


Your turn
You click “Place order.”
The spinner never stops.
Where do you start looking?
Browser console errors
Network tab: did the request even leave?
Server logs
A slow or locked database query
Payment provider timing out
Was the order created anyway?


One thing to take home
Be an investigator
Form a theory
→
Gather evidence
→
Narrow it down
→
Real cause
Not panic. Not random changes until it works.


Build it. Break it. Fix it.
